title: Rigidity of actions of connected algebraic groups on tori
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field]. All group schemes below are affine group schemes [def-sc-group-scheme] of finite type [def-weil-finite-type-morphism] over $k$, and all subgroup schemes are closed [def-sc-group-scheme-subgroup]. Smoothness is as in [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], and connectedness as in [def-weil-connected-scheme]; geometrically connected means connected after extension to an algebraic closure $\bar k$ of $k$. A torus is a group scheme becoming $(\mathbf G_m)^d$ over $\bar k$ for some integer $d\geq0$, where $\mathbf G_m$ is as in [def-sc-gm-ga]. Let $G$ be smooth and geometrically connected, let $T$ be a torus, and let $a:G\times_kT\to T$ be an action by group-scheme automorphisms. Thus for every commutative $k$-algebra $A$ and $g\in G(A)$, the map $t\mapsto a(g,t)$ is a group automorphism of $T(A)$, naturally under change of $A$. Then $a$ is the projection $G\times_kT\to T$; equivalently, $a(g,t)=t$ for all $A,g,t$.

source.place: Theorem 12.36 and Corollary 12.37, printed pp.243--244; specialization from groups of multiplicative type to tori.

proof.text: Write $K=\bar k$. It suffices to prove the equality after extension to $K$: if $C=k[T]$ and $D=k[G\times_kT]$, equality of the extended maps implies $(a^*(c)-\operatorname{pr}_2^*(c))\otimes1=0$ in $D\otimes_kK$ for each $c\in C$. [lem-sfb-field-extension-tensor-injective] makes $D\to D\otimes_kK$ injective. The spectrum correspondence [def-weil-affine-spectrum] and affine product formula [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] therefore imply equality of the original maps. Over $K$, choose the splitting $T_K\simeq\mathbf G_m^d$ supplied by the definition of torus in the statement, and conjugate the action by it. Put $X=G_K$. This is affine and connected by the hypotheses, and its identity is a $K$-point.

source.place: Theorem 12.36, reduction to algebraically closed k; Corollary 12.37, base-extension reduction made explicit.

proof.text: For each $n\geq1$ restrict the action to $X\times_KH_n$, where $H_n=(\mu_n)^d\subset\mathbf G_m^d$ [def-sc-gm-ga]. The homomorphism hypothesis makes this a family of homomorphisms $H_n\to\mathbf G_m^d$. [lem-sfb-finite-torsion-hom-parameter] gives its classifying morphism $c_n:X\to C_n$, with $C_n$ a finite disjoint union of copies of $\operatorname{Spec}K$. Each inverse image of a component is open and closed; connectedness forces exactly one to be nonempty [def-weil-connected-scheme]. The map factors through that open component, which is $\operatorname{Spec}K$, so it is the constant $K$-morphism with value $c_n(e)$. The action identity gives $a(e,h)=h$, hence naturality and injectivity of the classifying bijection give $a|_{X\times H_n}=\operatorname{pr}_2|_{X\times H_n}$ as scheme morphisms. This holds even when $\operatorname{char}K$ divides $n$.

source.place: Lemma 12.35 and Theorem 12.36, finite case; Corollary 12.37, evaluation at the identity.

proof.text: Put $B=\Gamma(X,\mathcal O_X)$. The affine product formula [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-product-affine-spectra] identifies $X\times_K\mathbf G_m^d$ with the spectrum of $L_B=B[t_1^{\pm1},\ldots,t_d^{\pm1}]$, and $X\times_KH_n$ with the spectrum of $L_B/(t_1^n-1,\ldots,t_d^n-1)$. Indeed [def-sc-gm-ga] gives the one-variable rings; iterate the affine product formula, and send $b\otimes t^u$ to $bt^u$. Its inverse sends a finite sum to $\sum b_u\otimes t^u$; the pure-tensor relations and the monomial multiplication show these maps are inverse. For $H_n$, impose each relation $t_i^n=1$; the inverse variables become $t_i^{n-1}$, giving precisely the displayed quotient. Thus the two pullbacks of every target function have the same image in every one of these quotients by Step 2.

source.place: Theorem 12.36, final paragraph on printed p.244: parameter-algebra tensor products, with their maps specified.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-torus-torsion-joint-injectivity] with coefficient ring $B$ and rank $d$. Step 3 gives $a^*(f)=\operatorname{pr}_2^*(f)$ for every target function $f$. The affine spectrum correspondence [def-weil-affine-spectrum] gives $a=\operatorname{pr}_2$ over $K$, and Step 1 gives the equality over $k$. Evaluating equal morphisms on any commutative $k$-algebra $A$ yields $a(g,t)=t$, as required.

source.place: Theorem 12.33 and Theorem 12.36, last paragraph, followed by Corollary 12.37.

proof_origin.place: Theorem 12.36 and Corollary 12.37, printed pp.243--244; finite case Lemma 12.35 and density Theorem 12.33.

lean.statement: theorem connected_action_torus_rigidity {k : Type u} [Field k] (G T : Grp (Over (Spec (.of k)))) [IsAffine G.X.left] [LocallyOfFiniteType G.X.hom] [QuasiCompact G.X.hom] [IsAffine T.X.left] [LocallyOfFiniteType T.X.hom] [QuasiCompact T.X.hom] [Smooth G.X.hom] (hG : ConnectedSpace ((MultiplicativeType.baseChange (K := AlgebraicClosure k)).obj G).X.left) (hT : MultiplicativeType.IsTorus T) [a : ModObj G.X T.X] (hhom : ∀ (A : CommAlgCat.{u} k) (g : (algSpec (.of k)).obj (op A) ⟶ G.X) (t₁ t₂ : (algSpec (.of k)).obj (op A) ⟶ T.X), g • (t₁ * t₂) = (g • t₁) * (g • t₂)) : a.smul = CartesianMonoidalCategory.snd G.X T.X
